Played the demo first and loved it. Very good mix of light base building and classic tower defense. Enemies attack buildings in their way instead of just gunning for the main base, which i usually don't like, but actually works really well with buildings healing between waves and the ability to build cheap walls. It forces you to think about where you can and cannot risk to expand for more income. Not sure how long the game will last, with the main content just being 4 difficulties on randomly generated maps. But I'm 100% sure i will be having a lot of fun until i beat all of those at least. So far I only did 1 run on the easiest difficulty (normal), both in the demo and in the full game. Those were fairly easy (as a veteran of the genre), but provided a bit of challenge still. Good run durations of around 1-2hrs per map. Harder difficulties should be even more fun!

Summary: Buy it. NOW. This game is highly polished, looks beautiful, sounds great, plays great, has rewarding meta-progression, and is very addictive. I did receive the game from the devs for free, but under no ogligation to review or say nice things about it. I surprisingly often get offered game keys and try them out on my YT channel but very rarely are they anywhere near this good. I'll be uploading a weeks worth of videos on this game because I couldn't stop playing and getting my score ever higher. It strikes a really good balance of difficulty scaling and still being fun. Once you get past wave 30 or so performance may start taking a serious hit due to the sheer numbers of bugs you have to kill, towers on the map, and effects. I recommend turning off damage numbers at that time and it'll reduce how much RAM it uses significantly. I managed to get to Wave 60 on the endless mode (you have to beat all of the other difficulties to unlock it) and it took 5 hours to complete because performance at that point was nearly non-existant. But to be clear I wouldn't expect even 1% of players to get that far, and I did lose from being defeated not from giving up due to the performance at that point. If you find it using a lot of ram (it was maxing out my 32GB of ram at that point) turn off damage numbers and restart the game every so often (it saves every wave so you can resume anytime). It's not often I write steam reviews but this one is a strong recommendation from me.
Was given a key so figured I'd feature it for a bit on my channel. Then couldn't stop playing it! Lots of replayability and scratches the roguelite itch!

I usually don't mind AI in games. I never would use it personally but again, don't really care. EXCEPT when it's it really seems like AI was used to CODE the game too. The game's settings options are clearly lazy. Not only that, they don't even work. - Resolution settings Similar to how developers designed it back during Windows XP days. Break beyond the intended aspect ratio/resolution size and you get Cursor Desyncs. Window-Fullscreen option is fake. it's just taking a fixed preset and adjusting it to native desktop. the bigger your native resolution, the more blurry. Windowed option is just terrible. it's a fixed tiny window. To actually make anyuse of this option you need to use AI or some program to rescale it for you such as Lossless Scaling for example. Fullscreen is just desycned if your resolution is too wide. Most of the time you can't even change the actual resolution as it's completely blank even if you line up the desynced cursor to properly interact with the resolution arrows. - FPS First starting the game it's fixed "off". Meaning, starting the game will turn your home into an airport with how loud your fans will get and lower spec systems will suffer harshly. Not having an SSD or decent size RAM and you're stuck for a while before you can fix that yourself. - Accessibility The settings for Accessibility are rather decent. But, basic. The default settings are horrible and even the size of the UI leaves a lot of unused space. It's almost as if the max setting of UI size was the intended size. not the 100% default size which looks like it's intended for an 800x600 monitor. Even the reduce visual effects accessibility is toggled on by default. If it's an accessibility choice, why is it defaulted on? The default setting should be "off" as that should be the dev's "intended experience" while Accessibility is a choice for those who may need it. I can keep going on with more of the settings. But, I tolerated enough of the game despite these issues and character limit is a thing. I'm refunding the game because far too much of the basics of every option in the game feels like it was intentionally ignored or coded completely by AI with no human intervention to clean things up and make it correctly functionable to a bare minimum expectation of functionality. Again, don't care about AI use. I do however care that the code for the game is so poorly done that far too much of basic core functionality to even start playing the game. uncomfortable setup with problems due to how terrible the settings in-game are, yet somehow worse than gaming on Windows XP era is not worth the current price tag and even if things change, this game is absolutely not for me even though there is a game to be played.

I've been having a great time with Axom so far. It does a really good job of mixing base building, tower defence, and roguelike progression into something that feels fresh and addictive. Every run gives you new choices and upgrades to experiment with, so it never feels like you're just repeating the same strategy over and over. Watching your defences come together while huge waves of enemies crash into them is incredibly satisfying. There's a ton of content and replayability. There are loads of buildings, upgrades, and research options to unlock, which makes each session feel rewarding even when things don't go according to plan. The gameplay loop is easy to get into but has enough depth to keep you thinking and adapting. If you're a fan of strategy games and enjoy building massive defensive setups, Axom is pretty cool

I love the game, I seriously do. One of the more entertaining, fun and deep Tower Defense games in a while. In a long while. I don't care about people brainlessly going on the fence about potential AI usage, or what engine a game runs on, or the level of graphics. I yearn for only two things: 1. A Tower Defense game that isn't medieval/magic themed, but sci-fi, and pulls it off nicely. I am absolutely tired of seeing the myriad of Tower Defense games that are using magic/medieval themes and stand out in absolutely no way. There are uncountable amounts of them on Steam, and they keep growing every month, without any soul. 2. Depth. My favourite genre will always be Tower Defense hybrids like Sanctum 2, because while placing towers and building mazes, you also have the added depth of playing it in FPS mode. But that doesn't restrict itself to hybrid gameplay, but literally any kind of longevity-providing factors. Infinitode 2 has hundreds of hours of depth due to infinite upgrades and upgrade scaling. Meta-Upgrades are defining the roguelite genre, and I fully like that. I like it when playing the game for a long time becomes a gameplay factor and not just something you can do. It's tough to pull off, naturally, as you don't want to have the game feel like you need to repeatedly lose runs before you can actually make a dent. This game pulls it off. The whole variety of options you have will easily carry you for ten hours. Meta-Upgrades too, if not twenty or more. In a way, Axom Conquest ticks off many of my boxes just the right way. Which makes tiny issues just the more frustrating, given how close the game is to being a perfect example of a well-rounded game of the genre. Issues: - I love the minions, however, they seem to become useless when the enemy doesn't move - the minion just sits there and watches, in knife-fight range, not doing anything. I had a flying bug destroy my nexus uncontested because the minion didn't do anything despite sitting ontop of the bug. - Laser Trip-Wire. Incredibly powerful in the early game, but abysmal to control. You need to connect two of them, but they only ever connect with the closest other Trip-Wire. If you build a perfectly symmetric defense ring around the nexus drill, where everything has even distances, you would think you would be able to form a nice rectangle with the lasers, covering all four sides. In reality, in the current game version, not so! Please give the Laser Trip-Wire an interface to manually set the connections, so you can tell it what other LTW to connect with. Inconvenience at using should not be the balancing factor for this otherwise very potent Hazard. - Hazard-focussed gameplay seems a bit weak in contrast to Tower-focussed gameplay, both in terms of range and total hazard count. I know Hazards are primarily supplements, but they feel like they should be options to Tower-focussed gameplay, at least with the Orange Nexus. For that matter I would slightly buff the amounts of all Hazards except the LTW, by at least one or two all across the board. Most maps allow for chokepointing, while on occasion you have very open maps that force you to sell upgraded Hazards just to cover other ground, as the enemy will spawn from any location and there seems to be no way to force a direction. It's a really cool game. I am really happy about the investment, and would recommend it to others. I hope you can find the time to keep polishing and upgrading the game, because raw diamonds deserve to be polished, and this diamond is almost perfect already!

Tough call. I’d recommend this game to fans of both tower defense and roguelike games, since the combination is fresh and the basic concept is really great. Overall, though, this game is only a 5/10. Unfortunately, this game suffers from some fundamental problems: Balancing: Some upgrades are ridiculously strong, while others are useless or even counterproductive. The same goes for the towers and, above all, for the RNG: Half of the maps are completely unplayable due to the layout of the high ground and resource spots. Bugs: I’ve lost runs multiple times because creeps simply glitched over cliffs. Rogue-lite: Most of the upgrades are trivial. I HATE the “get more currency” upgrade. But even simple “3% attack speed” upgrades are, in my opinion, just a waste of time. Overall, the upgrade system is too slow. Translated with DeepL.com (free version)

I think I've played just about every Tower Defense on Steam.... Axom does a great job of balancing what makes Tower Defense so fun, but also adds in some interesting wrinkles to mix things up. The enemy is constantly changing it's attacking positions, forcing you to make fresh, hard decisions each run. The maps seem random generated, and the towers are given to you in a roguelike manner, so it's virtually impossible to have a vanilla, go-to strategy. Of course you will have favorite approaches, but you will be forced to adapt throughout the run. I'm extremely impressed with the balance for such a young game: I'm 10 hours in, unlocked a next difficulty tier and feel like so far the balancing has been fantastic. I highly recommend to general fans of the genre, and really anyone looking for a casual, but challenging, strategy game.

This is a hidden gem. For an indie dev, everything is well made and there is thought put into towers and enemies and upgrades. You can see the dev wanted to make a good game, and they were successful. The graphics style is nice, and the game handles nicely large amount of enemies and projectiles (those who complain about performance and crashes are on amd cards which is unfortunate but if you got something else you won't see any crashes or problems). There's a lot to play here, even after 20 hours I haven't unlocked everything so you get your moneys worth for sure. You discover different upgrades and power ups every round so every round is different which keeps you going for another run. If I had to list some cons, its that there are clearly some things are stronger than others, but overall there are no useless towers. And there is lack of meaningful end goal; it's a roguelite TD so it's pretty much play the game as long as you think its fun. I would have liked there to be some sort of goal to go for that would give the feeling of "I beat the game" and then you could keep going for fun. You could say unlocking everything and beating hardest difficulty is end goal, but for me that isnt satisfying enough for end goal. For this price its a strong recommend. If it's on sale then its a steal.

In short Great mash-up tower defense with some rogue-like spice to keep it fresh. Games tough, but not impossible. Runs pretty smooth on a potato. Long Boi You're basically doing a smash and grab mission for resources. You crash land, set up a crude defenses, and then turn on the drill. Each time you drill the local (very zerg-like) wildlife says "naw-f that" and will attack your core drill and any satellite refineries. Combines a bunch of features from OG tower defense games as well as adding in some of its own flare. Some of these features are hidden behind capsules found during the round or by unlocking a new drill. It does force some meta progression as the later difficulties are near impossible without them. Some upgrades are completely essential to success. All in all, a great little time waster if you have 30 minutes to burn here and there. Manages to stay fresh with each run. 5/5

Nothing seems...unique enough with what I'm doing except some random thing that happens once along the waves. I don't know. Classes...benefits besides the nexus benefits. I don't know.
